analysis.title: GS Early Morning Research Recap: Ratings and Target Price Changes - November 5, 2026 as of 5:30 AM ET
key_insights: Two rating changes today, both outside the US: Saudi Tadawul Group (1111.SE) upgraded to Buy from Neutral on the view that trading volumes are at a cyclical trough and the non-volume tailwinds are structural. United Overseas Bank (UOBH.SI) downgraded to Sell from Neutral on more headwinds than tailwinds. No Americas rating changes.

Twelve Americas price target changes of 10% or more. Cuts: FIS to $35 from $44 after a big earnings reset, DOCN to $156 from $178, LUMN to $5 from $7.25, SEDG to $25 from $29, CLVT to $2.30 from $2.60, ITUB to $9.10 from $10.50. Raises: APP to $445 from $400, MMM to $225 from $200, CHYM to $43 from $38, PCOR to $90 from $70, TASK to $8 from $7, CAR to $108 from $94.
AppLovin Q3 revenue came in ahead of expectations. The note describes a return to strong revenue outperformance and focuses on execution against strategic growth opportunities.
Uber Q3 was a solid quarter with a forward guide. The note highlights an autonomous vehicle strategy update and an emphasis on secular growth and capital allocation.

Chime reported a Q3 beat and raise, with management pointing to a structurally higher growth rate going forward. FIS had a big earnings reset that sent shares lower. Remitly was in line with relatively soft 2027 preliminary guidance. Western Union expects a near-term rebound as cost savings offset structural compression.
Circle (CRCL) beat on top line and margin in Q3, but 4Q26 guidance implies a substantial quarter-on-quarter step down in RLDC margin.

ARM results were above the Street with positive AGI CPU commentary, but royalty revenue missed. Qualcomm is seeing datacenter momentum in a tepid smartphone market, with near-term margin headwinds. SiTime estimates are moving higher on datacenter and smartphone wins.

Solar names diverged. Shoals had a Q3 beat and raise that was overshadowed by the proposed ARRY merger. Array lowered guidance but reported a record order book. SolarEdge's near-term recovery was pushed out on US and Germany uncertainty, and GS keeps a Sell.

Energy: Cheniere had higher near-term estimates and a higher DCF and share target after Q3. European Big Oils show accelerated degearing and upgraded distributions, with freight rates and trading upside in focus for 4Q. GS flags early views on US state election results as a potential risk to Texas-exposed power names NRG and VST.
Chile copper labour negotiations add another supply risk into 2027, per GS Metals & Mining.

Consumer: Costco October sales beat expectations but traffic decelerated. e.l.f. Beauty reported a sizable FQ2 beat on topline strength and raised FY27 guidance as expected, with GS reiterating Buy. Home furnishings markdowns ticked down in 3Q. Kraft Heinz is likely to see limited earnings growth in FY27.

Zillow missed on EBITDA and lowered 2026 guidance on persistent housing market headwinds. Marriott Vacations disappointed on provisions, with an Investor Day as the next catalyst. Avis Budget stays a Sell, with sustainability of rental rate-per-day growth into 2027 a show-me story.

Industrials: Allegiant 3Q beat on revenue and 4Q outlook well ahead of expectations. 3M's broad PFAS settlement drives an initial re-rating with further upside potential. ATS missed in 2Q and lowered estimates on a weaker outlook. Maersk missed Q3 and revised guidance below expectations. Legrand posted a solid beat and raise.

Europe results: Tenaris had a strong 3Q beat with a 4Q step-up. Orsted beat EBITDA by 4% with guidance reaffirmed. Engie upgraded FY guidance. National Grid had a small H1 beat and raised FY guidance. Flutter downgraded FY26 guidance again on adverse sports results.

Asia: China consumer durables show overseas continuing to outperform domestic with a widening gap, and gross margin pressure is the major downside risk. GS stays Buy on Midea, Anker and Roborock. Xiaomi target cut to HK$35 from HK$39, VNET target cut to $4.60 from $14, Kstar target cut to Rmb38 from Rmb60.
Japan automakers: GS examines the share price reaction after the midterms. China authorities blocked the local sale of ABB Robotics.

Macro desk items listed: 4Q26 Treasury refunding recap, a slightly lower final 2026Q3 Japan real GDP tracking estimate with gradual recovery expected next year, an NZ election preview rated too close to call, and German defence spending driving a pick-up in equipment investment.
Upcoming GS events today include a Cross-Asset Hybrids webinar at 10:30 AM ET and an ISG session at 11 AM ET on Middle East escalation risks and US policy implications after the midterms.
